summary: The ask's premise is refuted: row 24 is NOT the OVA and its stored date is NOT wrong. Row 24 'The Carefree Cat' is 気ままな猫 (Kimama na Neko), the TV FINALE, and 2006-03-30 is its correct air date. The OVA the task was looking for is a DIFFERENT episode with a different Japanese title — 遠ざかる猫 Toozakaru Neko, 'The Distant Cat' (AniList 2589) — and it sits at OUR ROW 15, not 24. ja.wikipedia's 各話リスト states the whole structure explicitly: 話数 = 全24話（未放送1話）, the list numbers #15（未放送）遠ざかる猫 and then double-numbers every later row '#22（#23） 楽園の猫' and '#23（#24） 気ままな猫', with the footnote DVD版では、テレビ未放送の#15「遠ざかる猫」が新たに収録され、以降の話数が1話ずつ加算されている. Our row space is therefore the DVD numbering (24 slots), which is also AFL's and blackcat.fandom's numbering; the TV broadcast numbering (23 episodes, AniList 68) runs one LOWER from TV 15 onward. Rows 23 and 24 are both typed filler and stay unanchored under A1. No repair is proposed on row 24. The live question this lane surfaces is row 15 and the component span: AniList component 68 covers rows 1-23 while the series has 24 rows, so the last row is currently uncovered and the OVA is buried inside the episode list instead of being an order-only entry.

structure.notes:
IDENTITY OF ROW 24 — settled, three independent sources, all agreeing that 'The Carefree Cat' is the TV finale and not the OVA. 1. ja.wikipedia BLACK CAT, テレビアニメ infobox: 放送終了 = 2006年3月30日, 話数 = 全24話（未放送1話）. Its 各話リスト ends '| Number = #22（#23） | Title = 楽園の猫' then '| Number = #23（#24） | Title = 気ままな猫', i.e. TV episode 23 = DVD episode 24 = 気ままな猫 = 'The Carefree Cat'. The list's only unaired entry is '| Number = #15
（未放送） | Title = 遠ざかる猫', with the footnote 'DVD版では、テレビ未放送の#15「遠ざかる猫」が新たに収録され、以降の話数が1話ずつ加算されている' (the DVD adds the unaired #15 and increments every later episode number by one). 2. blackcat.fandom (MediaWiki API, action=parse&prop=wikitext): 'Episode 24: The Carefree Cat' — kanji 気ままな猫, romaji Kimama na Neko, air date March 30, 2006, prev = Episode 23, next = none (the finale). 'Episode 15: The Distant Cat' — kanji 遠ざかる猫, romaji Toozakaru Neko, air date '-' (never broadcast), prev = Episode 14, next = Episode 16. The wiki's 'List of Episodes' runs 1-24 with '-' as the airdate for 15 only and March 30, 2006 for 24. 3. animefillerlist: 24 rows, row 15 'The Distant Cat' dated 2006-07-26, row 23 'The Cat's Paradise' 2006-03-23, row 24 'The Carefree Cat' 2006-03-30 — the same DVD numbering our rows use (our stored 19-24 titles match AFL's wording exactly). 4. AniList 68 'Black Cat' format=TV, episodes=23, 2005-10-06 to 2006-03-30 — the TV run ENDS on 2006-03-30, which is precisely why row 24's stored date is right. AniList 2589 'Black Cat: Toozakaru Neko' format=OVA, 1 ep, 24 min, 2006-07-26 is the separate unaired episode. => The two titles were conflated in the ask: 気ままな猫 (carefree/whimsical) and 遠ざかる猫 (receding/distant) are different episodes. No G53 date repair. No title repair. Row 24 is correct as stored. THE REAL STRUCTURE FINDING — our row space is DVD numbering, and the OVA is row 15. Mapping between the two numbering spaces (join by title, never by index — R20): our/DVD/AFL/fandom 1-14 == TV 1-14 (unchanged) our/DVD 15 == the DVD-only unaired episode 遠ざかる猫 / 'The Distant Cat' (AniList 2589) — NO TV number our/DVD 16-24 == TV 15-23 (TV N = our N-1); our 23 'The Cat's Paradise' = TV 22 楽園の猫 (2006-03-23), our 24 'The Carefree Cat' = TV 23 気ままな猫 (2006-03-30) This is the same SOURCE_NUMBERING_SHIFTS shape already recorded for bungo-stray-dogs and seraph-of-the-end (where AFL numbers a post-finale OVA as an extra episode), except that here the insert is MID-RUN, so it shifts nine later rows rather than appending one. Consequences visible in our data: (a) entry aired_episodes = total_episodes = 24 while AniList's TV count is 23; (b) the sole component, AniList 68 [season], spans rows 1-23, so row 24 — a real TV episode — is covered by nothing, and rows 16-23 are mapped to the wrong TV episodes inside that span. TWO CLEAN DISPOSITIONS, for Sean to rule (no component placement made here, per the ask): (A) Keep DVD numbering (24 rows): extend component 68's span to 1-24 and record row 15 as the OVA (AniList 2589) with a numbering ruling that our N = TV N+1 from row 16 on. Matches AFL and blackcat.fandom, costs nothing to the stored rows, but leaves one component covering two AniList works. (B) Move to TV numbering (23 rows): retire row 15 to an order-only watch-order entry at @14.5 with kind `ova` and anilist_id 2589, renumber rows 16-24 down to 15-23. Matches AniList, ja-WP's primary numbering and the community count of 23, and makes component 68's existing 1-23 span correct as it stands. This is the shape the T29 order-only lane uses for every other bonus episode in the catalog. I have not proposed a repair for either, because the choice is a structure ruling and because both target rows (23, 24) are correct as stored under (A). A1 — WHY NEITHER TARGET ROW TAKES AN ANCHOR. Rows 23 and 24 are stored filler and AFL types them filler, as it does rows 21 and 22. The manga (AniList 30040, 20 volumes / 187 chapters) ends with Creed's defeat and an epilogue; the anime's last four episodes are the studio's own Eden/Kranz ending. Filler rows never carry chapter anchors (A1), so rows 23 and 24 take no anchor and no anchor_hostile entry — they take the A1 exemption stated here and in the summary. (This lane was scoped to identity, not placement: I did not re-derive the standings, and nothing I found contradicts them.)

flags_for_sean: PREMISE REFUTED — no repair on row 24. 'The Carefree Cat' = 気ままな猫 (Kimama na Neko) is the TV FINALE and 2006-03-30 is its correct air date; the OVA is 遠ざかる猫 Toozakaru Neko = 'The Distant Cat', a different episode, sitting at OUR ROW 15. ja-WP 各話リスト double-numbers the tail '#23（#24）気ままな猫' and marks '#15（未放送）遠ざかる猫'; blackcat.fandom's Episode 24 page gives air date March 30, 2006 with next = none, and its Episode 15 page gives air date '-'; AniList 68's TV run endDate is 2006-03-30. Sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/BLACK_CAT | https://blackcat.fandom.com/wiki/Episode_24:_The_Carefree_Cat | https://blackcat.fandom.com/wiki/Episode_15:_The_Distant_Cat | https://anilist.co/anime/68

CHECK ROW 15's STORED AIR DATE (I am read-only; the context listed only rows 19-24). Row 15 should be the DVD-only unaired episode 遠ざかる猫 / 'The Distant Cat'. It never aired on TV, so it has no broadcast date; AFL prints 2006-07-26 and AniList 2589 gives startDate 2006-07-26 for the OVA, while blackcat.fandom prints '-'. If our row 15 carries a March-2006 TV date it is wrong and a G53 air_date repair to 2006-07-26 is warranted — I did not file one because I could not observe the stored value. Sources: https://anilist.co/anime/2589 | https://www.animefillerlist.com/shows/black-cat | https://blackcat.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_Episodes

COMPONENT SPAN IS SHORT BY ONE ROW. The only component is AniList 68 [season] spanning 1-23, but the series has 24 rows, so row 24 ('The Carefree Cat', a real TV episode) is uncovered — and because the OVA occupies row 15, rows 16-23 inside that span are mapped to the wrong TV episodes. Ruling needed: (A) extend 68 to 1-24 and annotate row 15 as the OVA (AniList 2589), keeping DVD numbering; or (B) retire row 15 to an order-only entry @14.5 kind `ova` anilist_id 2589 and renumber 16-24 down to 15-23, which makes the existing 1-23 span correct and matches AniList / ja-WP / the community count of 23. I made no component placement, per the ask.

NUMBERING TRAP TO RECORD (same family as the mashle/bungo/seraph shifts): for black-cat, AFL, blackcat.fandom and our rows all use DVD numbering (24) while AniList and ja-WP's primary numbering use TV numbering (23), and the insert is MID-RUN at 15, so any index join between the two spaces silently mis-pairs nine episodes (our 16-24 vs TV 15-23) rather than just falling off the end. Join by title or by air date only.

NOT REVIEWED IN THIS LANE: whether row 15 ('The Distant Cat') should be typed canon — ja-WP and the fandom summary describe it as the Sephiria/Charden confrontation and Train receiving the orichalcum bullet, which is manga material, and AFL types it 'Manga Canon'. Its standing and any anchor are a placement question outside this identity ask; raising it only so the row is not assumed to be a bonus with no source content.
